processes.name: Daily credit report forwarding
processes.description: Credit group (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond, Darren Vanek) emails a daily credit report or pendings list to a long distribution list. Darron Giron forwards each one to a colleague (Carole Frank, later Ryan O'Rourke), apparently so his group sees counterparty rebook and pending actions.
processes.stall_points: Forwarded manually, often hours or days later (the 4/2 report is forwarded on 4/6, the 4/13 report on 4/16). The forward carries no added content, only the original attachment or body.
processes.automation: Auto-route the credit report to the group's shared mailbox or a distribution list at send time, and extract the counterparty rebook and pending actions into a tracked list.

processes.name: Sitara deal price and rate corrections
processes.description: Settlement/accounting staff compare counterparty invoices or confirmations against Sitara deal tickets and email the deal owner (Daren Farmer, Julie Meyers, Darron Giron) to verify and change the price or rate. The owner edits the ticket and replies, and billing then redrafts or invoices.
processes.stall_points: Requests wait on the one person who can edit the ticket. When Daren or Julie is out, the request is re-sent to a backup and the fix slips a day, against an invoice deadline.
processes.automation: Auto-compare invoice or confirmation price against the deal ticket and raise a price-mismatch task routed to the ticket owner or an on-duty backup, with the evidence attached.

processes.name: Deal ticket and meter fixes for volume management
processes.description: Logistics and volume-management staff correct deal tickets in Sitara and Unify (expired deals, zero-volume tickets, wrong desk entity, volume off by one) so volumes can be drafted, pathed and allocated. Each fix is raised by email to Daren Farmer or a peer.
processes.stall_points: Work stops when a deal ticket is expired, zero-volume or on the wrong entity, so people ask the owner for permission and wait. The same kind of ticket error recurs across months.
processes.automation: Flag expired, zero-volume or mismatched-entity tickets that have flow against them, and propose the ticket edit for the owner to approve with one click.

processes.name: Production vs nomination imbalance investigation
processes.description: Mary Poorman and colleagues compare month-to-date production with nominations and meter statements, find where volumes are over or under nominated, and fix nominations, trade zones or tickets. Imbalances also show up as OA variances that accounting then asks about.
processes.stall_points: Needs meter statements from the pipeline (faxed on request) and answers from several people. The same Big Cowboy gap recurs monthly and accounting questions the variance after the fact.
processes.automation: Automatically load pipeline meter statements and compare them with nominations and deal-ticket volumes each period, flagging meters with unmatched flow and the cumulative imbalance.

processes.name: Counterparty nominations, outages and on-call notes
processes.description: Logistics receives estimated actuals, nomination breakdowns, maintenance outages and on-call logs from counterparties (TXU, Equistar, Duke, Swift), and has to turn them into deal numbers and noms. The on-call log is emailed to the group.
processes.stall_points: Counterparty data arrives late or by email, in free text, and has to be matched to deal numbers by asking Daren. Estimated actuals get superseded once the real numbers come in.
processes.automation: Parse nomination and actuals emails into structured rows, match them to deal numbers, and prompt only for exceptions.

processes.name: Desk-lead information requests and chasers
processes.description: Auditors and support groups (Arthur Andersen quarter testing, curve validation, risk training topics, trader web-site access, exception reporting, headcount needs) email the gas desk leads for lists, explanations or status. Giron answers or forwards each request to his own team.
processes.stall_points: Requests go unanswered until a second reminder (Couch: only one response so far; McDowell: deadline already missed). Giron has to re-forward the same request to his group, and answers are sent back and then questioned again.
processes.automation: Track each request with owner and due date, auto-remind, and keep reusable answers (for example curve move explanations) so they are not re-asked.
